#1500. £329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham

Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on new players really does take some doing.

“Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

A team reimagined, a manager freshly launched and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

For Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he said. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”

Indeed he co-opted the Italian term “sbloccare” to describe his team’s problem. They simply need to unlock – or unblock – the team and the goals would flow. He joked that in Italy he would be lauded for two consecutive clean sheets in this game and the previous one against Nottingham Forest. “What did you write?” he demanded of one of the Italian newspaper correspondents. “You have the passport.”

Spurs have one last game at home this month, on Saturday against Aston Villa, to end the streak in September. They were into the second half before the first attempt on target that obliged Jordan Pickford to make a save – Mateus Fernandes’s shot slapping limply against the Everton goalkeeper’s gloves to ironic cheers from the home fans.

“There is a term in Italian, ‘sbloccare’ that literally translates as ‘unblock’… I know we can score goals and win games. We have to respect the history of the players – if you forget [Dominic] Solanke and [Omar] Marmoush the others haven’t scored many in their careers. I think we can find the goals with the quality of the players.”

Spurs play Liverpool at Anfield in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday before Villa a week today. The Spurs record at home is dismal. In the last 35 games they have won just five, drawn 10 and lost a remarkable 20. This new stadium has become a problem for the team in it – or maybe it is the other way around.

A good result for Everton, who were under pressure for most of the first half but had much the better of it after the break. David Moyes’s team finished the game with more shots on target than the home team. Moyes managed the game well and trusted his team to withstand the Spurs possession in the first half until they reached a point where Everton could start to push back.

Hard to pick out any major chances – it was that kind of game – but Brennan Johnson should have won it for the away team in the second half. The ball was cut back to him by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and the former Spurs man skied his shot.

Some surprised faces then when Moyes said later that he had expected a lot more from his team. He acknowledged the resilience in defence and the importance of the clean sheet. “We played well enough,” he said, “but when we had the ball we turned it over more often than we should have done.”

The game had started with Vitaliy Mykolenko being tortured by the pace of Sávio and ended with the Ukrainian left-back being given the man of the match award. Like many of his team-mates, he had hung in there. There was another fine performance from Jarrad Branthwaite at centre-half and Moyes said that he hoped it might earn him a place in the England squad. “He is still finding his way back from injury,” Moyes said, “it would be great if he could get a call-up.”

In the directors’ box were the usual pained expressions of Vinai Venkatesham, the Spurs chief executive, and chairman Peter Charrington. They sat alongside Vivienne Lewis, daughter of the patriarch Joe. There is a certain fatigue about the home crowd when faced with afternoons like this which suggests they have seen so much that the bar is quite high – or low – to provoke a really splenetic response. Perhaps it is just too early in the season although the final whistle was met with boos.

The first shot on target of the entire game for either side was a free-kick struck by James Garner in added time at the end of the first half. Spurs had started at a ferocious pace although they could not sustain it.

De Zerbi complained about the pre-season injuries on tour in Australia and also the lack of time he had to integrate Sávio and Marmoush. He said that his team were not in the right “physical condition”.

“We played very well in the first 30 minutes and maybe the energy and the fact we didn’t score – we lost confidence.” By the end, he had sent on James Maddison, Tel, Lucas Bergvall and Mohammed Kudus to little avail. Everton looked more likely to win it.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Everton defender said: “You look at the game from the start, they put us under pressure and we had to dig deep to stay in the game. Then we grew into the game towards the end of the first half and showed that mentality again in the second half.

“We had chances to win the game as well. The backs to the wall mentality will help us go a long way. If we can keep clean sheets, you can go a long way in the league. But it’s not just us the defenders. It’s the whole team working hard. It’s a team effort.”

"I feel like we could've taken three points" James Tarkowski speaks after his sides draw with Spurs 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/Wdj3N5hk8l

"Six hours and we've not scored a goal? It's a DISGRACE" 😬Ashley Young says that the Spurs players will need to have conversations about their lack of threat going forward ❌ pic.twitter.com/0KNomGEavx

"Absolutely diabolical" 😬Jamie Redknapp on Spurs not scoring in their first four Premier League games 😳 pic.twitter.com/48Nbxymlev

Tottenham failed to take the attacking initiative or create any notable chances. De Zerbi used multiple forward players in a host of attacking positions, but no one could find the breakthrough.

Boos ring around the ground as Spurs and Everton both have to settle for a point. Tottenham’s winless start to the season continues, while Everton’s unbeaten run remains intact. Spurs haven’t managed a goal in six hours of Premier League football across the 2026-27 campaign. Tottenham sit 17th with two points. Everton are up to seventh and will certainly take the draw.

FULL-TIME: The points are shared between Spurs and Everton at Tottenham Hotspur stadium 🤝 pic.twitter.com/HwPuKI3Ajh

Dewsbury-Hall’s deflected effort flies out for a corner. Everton can’t make the most of the resulting set piece and Tottenham survive.

There will be three minutes of added time. Are we set for late drama at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium?

Pickford makes an error as his poor clearance is intercepted by Maddison. The ball is eventually worked to Bergvall, whose curling effort is parried away by the Everton goalkeeper.

Jordan Pickford gets down well to deny Lucas Bergvall! 🧤 pic.twitter.com/59uoHTqto6

Tosin comes on for his Spurs debut as he replaces Gray. Can anyone be Tottenham’s hero and find a late winner?

Garner is booked after he clatters into Savio. Everton have produced a tough and disciplined defensive perfomance so far.

Spurs are now enjoying a sustained period of possession. They’re waiting to fashion a big chance and end their wait for a top-flight goal in the 2026-27 season.

De Zerbi makes another change as Maddison enters the action with applause from the Spurs faithful. He replaces Marmoush. It looks like Tel is now operating as a false nine.

Johnson misses a huge chance! Dewsbury-Hall fires a low cross into his path and Johnson takes the chance with a first-time shot, but he slices his effort and it goes over the bar. He’s got to do better from that range inside the penalty area.

That opportunity is Johnson’s last action of the match as he comes off for Hackney. O’Brien is also introduced, replacing Maitland-Niles.

That was the chance. Dewsbury-Hall rolls it into the path of Spurs’ Europa League final winner Brennan Johnson and he skied it. He hasn’t scored since he left Spurs in January for Palace.

"What a chance this was!"Brennan Johnson had the chance to put Everton in front against his former club 😯 pic.twitter.com/fUi7t6hX7t

Everton look like the far likelier side to break the deadlock. De Zerbi’s changes have done little to affect the game. Marmoush is cutting a very frustrated figure up top for Spurs.

Bergvall finds Savio with a whipped cross. The winger tries to help the ball back into the danger zone, but Pickford reacts quickly and collects possession.

Dewsbury-Hall picks up the game’s first yellow card after catching Tonali with a late sliding challenge.

What is Kinsky doing?! The goalkeeper’s dreadful pass which was intended for Tonali is intercepted by Dewsbury-Hall, who tries to slide a low effort through Kinsky’s legs. The Tottenham man redeems himself with a crucial save to keep the scoreline goalless. The hosts are living so dangerously. Kinsky needs to wake up.

Antonín Kinský redeems himself after Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall fails to take advantage! 😮 pic.twitter.com/nuKZju90Wz

Moyes responds with a straight swap on the wing as Grealish comes on for George.

Enter: Grealish. He is on for Tyrique George. Surprised that Brennan Johnson survived that change. He has struggled to make an impression.

Following Spurs’ reshuffle, it looks like Savio will stay out wide on the right, with Tel on the left. Kudus will sit as the central playmaker behind Marmoush, who is now the lone frontman.

De Zerbi orders a much-needed triple change as Kudus, Tel and Bergvall replace Solanke, Fernandes and Bentancur.

Jack Grealish has long since stopped the warm-up on the touchline and is now just staring at the game in expectation of his introduction.

A couple of chances for Everton. Spurs have survived but they look so vulnerable when Everton turn over possession. Crowd could turn soon. Almost reached the hour-mark on matchday 4 and still no Spurs’ Premier League goal.

The start of Spurs’ second-half performance is alarmingly similar to their display against Newcastle two weeks ago. That day, Tottenham allowed Newcastle to seize the initiative and they netted two second-half goals without reply. Everton are gaining confidence as Spurs continue to lack courage or threat. The crowd is getting more and more restless.

Tottenham fail to clear a corner and the ball lands at George’s feet. The Everton winger shoots but his fierce drive is blocked by Bentancur. The whole of Spurs’ bench is warming up. The visitors currently have the momentum and the hosts look nervous.

Everton are looking threatening once again as George attempts to thread a pass through to Johnson on the counter-attack, but Van de Ven is there to clear.

George does brilliantly to escape away from Gray and floats a cross towards the back post. Barry rises highest and his close-range header is blocked by Kinsky. The Tottenham goalkeeper didn’t know much about it, but that’s a massive stop. Undoubtedly the game’s most dangerous moment in front of goal so far.

Spurs’ first shot has arrived! Unfortunately, Fernandes’ tame long-range effort is easily gathered by Pickford. There were some sarcastic cheers from the Tottenham fans as Fernandes took aim. They clearly want more attacking inspiration from their players.

Ironic cheers as Spurs have their first shot on target. It has taken them until the start of the second half and it would be hard to say Fernandes stung the palms of Pickford.

We are back under way for the second half. Everton and Spurs are both unchanged at the break. With the anxiety building in the stadium as the game remains goalless, how long will De Zerbi wait before making a change?

An uneventful first half of football comes to a close. In a game lacking rhythm, creativity and attacking spark, nothing separates Tottenham and Everton at the break. Spurs’ search for a first Premier League goal this season continues.

There will be two added minutes. Everton have a free kick on the edge of Spurs’ penalty area. Garner and Dewsbury-Hall are standing over it. The former Manchester United and Nottingham Forest midfielder takes it and his effort bounces in front of Kinsky, who pushes it out for a corner.

James Garner free-kick pushed away by Kinsky is the game’s first attempt on target.

There has not been a single attempt on target at 40:27 from either team. Spurs have had the best of it but even so. That’s a poor return.

Another attack fizzles out for Spurs. Substitute Jack Grealish engaging in some badinage with home fans as he warms up. He famously agreed a move to Spurs in 2018, called off at the eleventh hour when Aston Villa were sold to the current ownership.

That is so poor from Fernandes. The summer signing’s overhit corner drifts out for a goal kick. Suddenly, Spurs’ attacking play has fallen quite flat.

Pickford does well to intercept Robertson’s inviting low cross. The left back needed Solanke or Marmoush to make a darting near-post run there to give him more options.

Spurs are bossing this game but on the rare occasions Everton escape you do wonder if they might score.

Tottenham are roared on by the home support to move the ball a bit quicker going forward. Out of possession, Everton almost revert to a back five, with Garner dropping very deep near to Tarkowski and Branthwaite.

Tonali picks out Gray with a pinpoint pass. Garner is alert to the danger and tracks back to clear, stopping Gray from getting a one-on-one opportunity.

Maitland-Niles does very well to dispossess Tonali in a dangerous area, allowing Barry to tee up Dewsbury-Hall, but his shot is smothered by the Spurs defence. Mykolenko then chips a cross into a box, but it’s tapped behind for a corner by Robertson. Moyes will certainly be encouraged by this side’s resurgence over the last 10 minutes.

There is a break in play here with Gray down and receiving treatment after a collision. He appears to be holding his lower back. The Tottenham man gingerly gets back to his feet and trudges off the pitch.

Gray down for some extended treatment. Richarlison in the stands. Spurs in danger of losing early momentum.

After Spurs’ fast start, Everton have grown into the contest over the last five minutes and are getting on the ball far higher up the pitch.

Garner’s corner is cleared by Spurs, but only as far as Maitland-Niles. In similar range to where he scored that stunning equaliser against Manchester United, the former Arsenal man shoots, but his attempt fizzes well wide.

Spurs are really flowing here. Finding the balls through the lines and real speed when they attack Everton. Big question is whether they can convert that into goals. Van Hecke and Fernandes both had chances.

Sávio has had a fine start to the game. Mykolenko in for a long afternoon. Spurs have looked dangerous and should be 1-0 up.

Tonali finds Savio with a deep cross, leaving Pickford in no-man’s land. The Brazilian keeps the ball in play and it loops up, just out of Marmoush’s reach.

Robertson floats a teasing delivery into Van Hecke at the back post, but the centre-back directs his half-volley over the bar from close range.

Spurs then burst forward again through Savio, who feeds Fernandes. The playmaker’s low drive is heroically blocked by Tarkowski as Everton continue to hold on (just about).

As expected, it’s Tottenham with all the early possession, with Everton sitting very deep and soaking up the early pressure. Marmoush turns Armstrong and wins a free-kick in a dangerous area.

They’re under way in north London, the hosts are in their lily-white and navy kit, with Everton in their grey/dirty green (is that a colour?!) away number.

Greetings from N17. It’s a wonderful, warm late summer evening. As expected there is the usual foreboding from the home fans. Two defeats and one draw. The mood will sour further if Spurs do not win today. No Porro or Udogie so Archie Gray, ever adaptable, starts at right-back again.

Everton are undefeated with five points from three games. They have a decent 16/17 players but it is the reserves beyond that which everyone is concerned about. Grealish and Dibling on the bench give them two potential game-changers. Spurs’ squad looks very strong on the team-sheet. A full bench of experienced pros and no fillers. On the pitch it has been less convincing.

"Solanke is a crucial player"Roberto De Zerbi on the importance of Dominic Solanke being fit for Spurs 💪 pic.twitter.com/FNWNsTWdt8

Coventry City vs Brighton & Hove Albion (14:00)

Manchester United vs Manchester City (16:30)

Brennan Johnson spent two years at Tottenham and scored the winning goal in the 1-0 Europa League final victory over Manchester United in May 2025, ending the club’s 17-year trophy drought.

After a short, disappointing spell at Crystal Palace, Johnson joined Everton last month, with Dwight McNeil moving in the opposite direction.

The Welsh winger starts for Everton today. Could he hurt his previous employers on a day where they desperately need a win?

Brennan in the building. 💙 pic.twitter.com/94GgAY8c56

Midfielder took exception to negativity surrounding club after moves for players on deadline day failed to materialise.

“We signed Jack [Grealish], which was nice, and I’d been speaking to him,” says Dewsbury-Hall, sitting in a café at the club’s Finch Farm training base. “But I had seen all the stuff [online], all the meltdowns about this and that and, in all honestly, it annoyed me a bit.

“I get where people are coming from. Everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad, but there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded. I was seeing people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’

“What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go. That’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room.”

Earlier this week, Mykhailo Mudryk picked up an ankle injury in training which has ruled the Chelsea loanee out of action for as long as two months.

The winger only made his debut for Tottenham as a late substitute against Nottingham Forest last week, but his attempt to rebuild his career following his anti-doping ban has been dealt a major blow.

Folarin Balogun’s proposed £39m move from Monaco collapsed on transfer deadline day, Richarlison’s return to the club didn’t materialise and Beto was sold to Fiorentina, leaving Thierno Barry as Everton’s only recognised striker.

Nottingham Forest’s pursuit of academy product Harrison Armstrong ruffled the fans’ feathers, while Iliman Ndiaye was sold to Manchester City for £60m.

Dwight McNeil, Tim Iroegbunam, Nathan Patterson, Adam Aznou and Idrissa Gueye were also allowed to leave.

Merlin Rohl and Tyrique George made their loans permanent, while Brennan Johnson, Hayden Hackney and Christian Norgaard were also added to the squad.

Summer signing Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Vitaliy Mykolenko are David Moyes’ only options at full-back.

Overall, there were a number of solid additions, just not enough of them to cover all the departures.

🎧🫡 Thierno Barry ahead of today's clash in North London. pic.twitter.com/mwlsKH8Pid

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van de Ven, Van Hecke, Robertson; Tonali, Bentancur, Fernandes; Savio, Solankem, Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Tel, Bergvall, Kudus, Davies.

Everton: Pickford; Maitland-Niles, Tarkowski, Brathwaite, Mykolenko; Armstrong, Garner; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry.

Subs: Travers, O’Brien, Keane, King, Alcaraz, Graham, Hackney, Dibling, Grealish.

After scoring that last-minute leveller against Manchester United last time out, Ainsley Maitland-Niles is promoted to the starting 11 and replaces Merlin Rohl. Brennan Johnson returns to his former club and starts, while Jack Grealish is on the bench.

Today's Toffees to face @SpursOfficial. COYB! ✊#TOTEVE pic.twitter.com/mOcCayRUfm

Roberto De Zerbi has made four alterations from last weekend’s stalemate with Nottingham Forest. Dominic Solanke, Mateus Fernandes, Archie Gray and Andy Robertson all come into the line-up. Pedro Porro and Destiny Udogie are out injured, while Conor Gallagher and Mathys Tel are relegated to the bench. Tosin Adarabioyo and James Maddison are also among the substitutes.

Our Spurs side to take on Everton 👊🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/n637s7swiD

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Everton in the capital.

Are Tottenham in must-win territory already? It may seem reactionary and premature, but after spending £380m in the summer to revamp an underperforming squad, Tottenham sit inside the relegation zone, with just one point and zero goals scored in three games.

Roberto De Zerbi’s men opened the 2026-27 top-flight season with worrying back-to-back defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United, before ending their losing streak last weekend thanks to a goalless draw against Nottingham Forest.

This game gives Tottenham another opportunity to reverse their dreadful home form. Last season, Spurs managed just three league wins at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and lost 10. The recent 2-0 loss against Newcastle was a painful reminder of Spurs’ shortcomings at home, but they’ll be expected to be authoritative and seize the initiative here today. A much-needed three points would be the perfect remedy to ease the pressure and unwanted attention on De Zerbi and his squad.

Meanwhile, Everton have made an unbeaten start to the season, accumulating five points from their first three league matches. David Moyes’ side looked set for defeat last time out, when they were trailing Manchester United 2-1 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium heading into stoppage time, until Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ stunning 96th-minute equaliser salvaged a draw.

Alongside drama on the pitch, there has also been noise off it. A bizarre transfer window has left Everton with a serious lack of depth up top and in both full-back positions. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responded to the fans’ negativity over this situation, saying their meltdowns “annoyed” him.

Nevertheless, they arrive in North London with all eyes on Tottenham and if the hosts can find a first league victory this season.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1499. Jack Grealish can't turn down a good night out and his attitude is a problem. IAN HERBERT reveals how the magnetic maverick star sparked concern and now faces a tragedy of missed opportunity

By IAN HERBERT, DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 22:00 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 09:57 EDT, 2 November 2026

At the Pride of Britain awards a week back, we witnessed the brilliant and magnetic side of Jack Grealish, sprinkling stardust as he presented an award to a child of unimaginable courage who counts the Everton player as his hero. 'Footballers are classed as heroes – but these are the real heroes,' Grealish said that night. You could have heard a pin drop.

It was no different when he arrived back at Everton in September, to the delight of the kids awaiting him and his white Lamborghini in the country lane outside the club's Finch Farm training base. 'It feels so good. I think I'm at my best at everything in life when I feel loved,' Grealish said, articulating a very real sense that he was coming home.

He is popular around the club because it can be said without fear of exaggeration that he has a heart of gold.

Only on Thursday, an Everton-supporting father-of-three with a cancer diagnosis that gives him weeks to live disclosed that Grealish had put £10,000 his way. But within hours of that simple act of altruism coming to light, evidence of the other Grealish emerged, as Everton announced he had been excluded from the squad to face Newcastle in the Carabao Cup for failing to turn up for training last week.

It was by no means the first time. Everton sources say there had been similar causes for concern last season. Grealish reported sick ahead of last weekend's game at Arsenal, shortly after the Pride of Britain awards, and has breached Everton's disciplinary code through an unauthorised absence. The stated reason for his absence at Arsenal was illness.

Jack Grealish remains popular at Everton and has a heart of gold, shown by a £10,000 gift to a fan suffering from cancer, but he has since been dropped over a breach of discipline

There were similar causes for concern last season, with his return this summer going against David Moyes' better judgement

Everton's owners, looking for Grealish's glitz and glamour to gloss over their desperately poor and unambitious summer in the transfer window, were keen to bring him back. It was against David Moyes' own better judgement that he accepted his return as part of the deal that brought Iliman Ndiaye's unwelcome departure to Manchester City.

Moyes needed discipline in a thin squad where every player's contribution would count this season. It was an opportunity for the few star players to inspire and shine a light for the younger ones. And therein lies the tragedy of missed opportunity where Grealish is concerned.

He, the quintessential British maverick playmaker in the mould of George Best and Alan Hudson, could be a Goodison hero of these days, yet seems incapable of showing he is bothered, ridding himself of the acolytes and hangers on who are dragging him down, and appreciating what an opportunity football offers him.

Though he likes a drink, it's not so much booze as his attitude, and a struggle to turn down a good night out, which is contributing.

There is no doubt that he still has the skills to be a cherished player. That much was clear in the early stages of last season when he was providing more assists than any other Everton player until a broken foot requiring surgery brought a premature end to his season.

This season he has, as yet, no assists. He has perhaps been frustrated at the number of chances he has created not being converted, though not every winger has Erling Haaland as his support act.

Grealish's patchy attitude to a football life is affecting his game, as he is not taking his man on in the way he used to and does not emit such light on the wing

Look hard enough, though, and you'll see signs that his patchy attitude to a football life is affecting his game. He is not taking his man on in the way he used to and does not emit such light on the wing. Pep Guardiola, at Manchester City, was the first to see this and rapidly made it clear he wanted him gone.

It's not too late for the 31-year-old to become the totemic presence that so many fervently want him to be on Merseyside. Moyes, who sees the wasted potential, has given him abundant support and patience since City left him out in the cold, hoping that he can make him see the opportunity, here.

Thursday night's excellent Carabao Cup win over Newcastle United opens up the potential for an exciting Cup run, with Fleetwood Town awaiting in the quarter-finals. Everton have not won a trophy for 31 years.

The hope must be that the significantly public nature of Grealish's omission – very much a case of Moyes refusing to tolerate another breach – will shock him into action.

It was even the wish of Prime Minister Andy Burnham, present at Thursday night's match, that Grealish would be re-signed to Everton and the PM declared after meeting him at the Pride of Britain awards that the player was an example of the way people 'buy into Everton.'

The collective wish for him to thrive at the club could not be clearer. Only he can make that happen.

#1498. Lecce vs Juventus: in-form hosts await Spalletti’s stretched side at the Via del Mare

Juventus face Lecce at the Stadio Via del Mare this evening, and the fixture arrives at an awkward moment for Luciano Spalletti. His side are still looking for a first win since the 3-0 home defeat by Lazio, while Di Francesco’s Lecce come into Matchday 8 on the back of their most convincing result of the season.

Kick-off is at 18:00 Italian time, which is 17:00 in the UK and Ireland.

Lecce travelled to Udinese last weekend and came away with a 3-0 victory. According to Flashscore, Kialonda Gaspar headed in the opener from a Gallo corner in the 14th minute, and N’Dri doubled the lead in the 25th minute after Tiago Gabriel had gone up for a header. Siebert added the third four minutes from time after a ball was won from Ekkelenkamp.

It was Lecce’s first win in Udine for six years and handed Udinese a fifth straight league defeat. Fatah also hit the crossbar, so the margin could have been even wider. For a side that has spent much of its recent history fighting at the wrong end of the table, it was a timely lift before the visit of Juventus.

The picture is very different in Turin. The heavy home loss to Lazio was followed by a 2-2 draw with Rennes in the Europa League, and the injury list has kept growing. Zeki Celik and Nico Gonzalez are the latest names to drop out, as covered in our Celik and Nico Gonzalez injury update, and Spalletti chose not to give a pre-match press conference on Saturday.

The Lazio defeat in Turin left Juventus well short of the Serie A leaders, so Sunday is about more than one result. Three points in Puglia would ease some of the pressure that has built up over the past week.

Juventus do not have to look far back for a good memory of this trip. The club’s own retrospective recalls the Matchday 36 meeting at the Via del Mare in May 2026, when Dusan Vlahovic scored after just 12 seconds. Kenan Yildiz started the move, Teun Koopmeiners was involved in the build-up and Andrea Cambiaso delivered the ball for Vlahovic to finish into the roof of the net.

That game stayed lively. Michele Di Gregorio had to make a fine save at the other end, Francisco Conceicao struck the crossbar and Vlahovic had another good chance, all inside the first six minutes. Pierre Kalulu thought he had added a second with around half an hour to play, but VAR ruled it out for a marginal Vlahovic offside in the build-up. The early goal proved enough for the win.

Several of the players involved that day, including Yildiz and Conceicao, are now injured, which shows how much Spalletti’s options have changed since May.

Tuttosport reports that Maresca will referee the match. In Italy it is live on DAZN and Sky. In the United Kingdom the game is shown on DAZN UK and Prime Video UK, in Ireland on DAZN, and in the United States on Paramount+, fuboTV and Peacock, according to the club’s broadcast guide.

Sources: Juventus FC, Juventus FC broadcast guide, Flashscore

At Juve FC, Luca covers match analysis, squad news, and the longer threads that run through a Juventus season. He writes with the perspective of someone who genuinely cares about where the club is heading rather than simply reporting what has already happened. His focus tends to lean toward how the team sets up, where things break down, and what needs to change to get back to where Juventus belongs in the European conversation.

#1497. Bayern Munich: Harry Kane names the strongest moment of his season

For Harry Kane, the 2025-2026 season has been marked by several breakthrough performances, but one evening holds a special place. In his interview given to France Footballthe 2026 Ballon d’Or designated his hat-trick in the final of the German Cup, won 3-0 against VfB Stuttgart, as one of the high points of his exercise. Bayern Munich had been waiting to regain this trophy for six years and the English striker had made the difference in a major meeting. “That final was probably one of my greatest performances. I took my responsibility by scoring a hat-trick”he explained.

Kane also cited England’s victory against the Democratic Republic of Congo (2-1) in the round of 16 of the World Cup, during which he scored his team’s two goals in the 75th and 86th minutes. A memory all the more striking for him in view of the previous English disillusionments in the knockout matches. “Being the one who took responsibility that day and allowed the team to qualify gave me one of the greatest emotions of my life”he admitted. Two decisive meetings which illustrate the importance of his goals in the moments when his team needed him the most.

#1496. Tuttosport: Foster could follow Battersea Power Station lead to preserve San Siro – the idea

It is possible that the plans for the existing San Siro – once the new stadium is constructed – could change slightly.

Milan and Inter unveiled the Generali Stadium last Thursday, which will be the new 71,500-seat stadium for the two clubs, but the future of their current home is still uncertain according to Tuttosport (via MilanPress).

The idea was to demolish a large part of the San Siro, keeping standing only a south-east portion, around 30% of the external ramps. A piece of the Curva Sud would be preserved and a part of the orange stand, areas that will be used for new purposes.

Some politicians – especially Senate President Ignazio La Russa – have always maintained that demolition isn’t necessary even with the new stadium. This concept has never been discussed by the two clubs or the council, but it could serve as an example to follow.

The paper adds that Norman Foster – one of the design architects behind the Generali Stadium – has declared that he wants to preserve a larger part of San Siro. It could follow the route of one of the previous projects in which he took part at Battersea Power Station in London.

Frank Gehry y Norman Foster construirán la fase final de Battersea Power Station. http://t.co/odgwaii4nz pic.twitter.com/1zyFjMu8P1

The building was restored by WilkinsonEye, but Foster’s studio played a key role in the area redevelopment with the Battersea Roof Gardens and 50 Electric Boulevard.

#1495. Douglas Luiz finally opens his Juventus account as Spalletti hails display at Lecce

Douglas Luiz has finally scored for Juventus. The Brazilian midfielder found the net in Sunday’s 2-0 win at Lecce, more than two years after his €50m move from Aston Villa, and he also set up the opening goal for Weston McKennie.

It was a night that changed the conversation around a player who has spent much of his time in Turin under scrutiny. Luciano Spalletti was quick to single him out afterwards, and the club’s own numbers show just how rare an evening like this has been for him.

According to the standout stats published by Juventus on Monday, this was the first time Douglas Luiz had both scored and assisted in the same match in Europe’s top five leagues. Before Sunday he had made 261 appearances in those competitions without managing it.

The club also points out that he now has two goal involvements from eight Serie A appearances this season, one goal and one assist. In the 2024/25 campaign he played 19 league games for Juventus and failed to register either.

Both contributions came before the break. His free kick was dinked over the Lecce defence for McKennie to break the offside line and slide in on 29 minutes. Twelve minutes later, Federico Gatti laid the ball off and Douglas Luiz hit it first time from outside the box into the far corner.

Douglas Luiz’s first goal in Bianconero! ⚪⚫ pic.twitter.com/g2vTIhUEnF

JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 25, 2026

The midfielder did not dwell on the personal milestone. In comments shared by the club’s press room after the game, he put the result first.

“The most important thing today was to win. I’m really happy with the result because we’ve worked so hard, and I’m delighted for the team. This victory also gives us the confidence we need,” he said.

He was also honest about the second half, when Lecce pushed Juventus back. “We played well in the first half, but I think we could definitely have done better in the second. We need to improve and perform well for the full 90 minutes.”

Speaking to DAZN, he added that the set piece routine involving Teun Koopmeiners is something the squad practises a lot, and that the players were pleased for their coach after a difficult week, as Tuttosport reported.

Spalletti had already explained after the 3-0 defeat by Lazio that he wanted changes, as covered in our piece on the changes Spalletti identified. Since then Juventus have moved to a three-man midfield, and Douglas Luiz has been one of the beneficiaries.

Speaking to Sky Sport Italia, the coach was full of praise for the Brazilian. “He had a great game today, he fought and ran, he battled on all sides and he helped clean up certain situations when we needed him to,” Spalletti said, in quotes reported by Football Italia.

He came off after 82 minutes, replaced by Sarr, having done the bulk of the work in a side that had only 17 outfield players available. With Manuel Locatelli and Khéphren Thuram among the absentees listed in our latest injury update, Spalletti needs exactly this kind of reliability from his remaining midfielders.

One good night does not settle a debate that has followed Douglas Luiz since his arrival. What it does give him is a platform. If he can keep producing this level of energy and quality in a system that suits him, the midfielder who struggled to make an impact in his first season may yet become an important figure for Spalletti this term.

Sources: Juventus FC, Football Italia, Tuttosport

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.

#1494. GdS: Milan enjoying the ‘best ever’ version of Rabiot – renewal imminent as figures emerge

Adrien Rabiot continues to dazzle with his performances and goal contributions, which AC Milan intend to reward him for.

La Gazzetta dello Sport confirm that the discussions between Rabiot and Milan have been underway for some time regarding an ‘update’ to the terms of his contract. Gerry Cardinale has very clear ideas about his priorities, and the Frenchman is next on the list.

In recent months, several players have ascended to the fourth floor of Casa Milan to sign extensions. There have been the young talents (Camarda and Comotto, 2031), veterans (Modric, 2027) and core pieces within the squad (Pavlovic, Pulisic, 2031).

Rabiot clearly belongs to the latter category (but also to a certain extent the same one as Modric) and has become the most urgent task to complete in terms of contracts.

The parties are in fact talking based on a shared desire to move forward together. For Cardinale, Rabiot represents one of the pillars on which the team’s rebuilding will continue.

Rabiot is seen as a player with the wisdom of experience, a perfect example for the younger players, and someone with the qualities of a leader even without the captain’s armband. Milan want to get back to the top, by Cardinale’s admission, and they need players like Adrien to help the cause.

So, a contract extension until 2030 has been ready for him for some time now (his current one expires in 2028). After the summer Napoli rumours, Rabiot remained at Milan partly because of his existing deal, but also partly because Cardinale convinced him.

What happens now? The next crucial step will be with his mother. Indeed, it is Mrs. Véronique who manages the former PSG midfielder’s interests, and a meeting will take place shortly. A pay rise from €3.5m net per season to €5m per year – what Pulisic earns – seems reasonable to presume.

With Rabiot on nine goal contributions for the season (five goals, four assists) he needs just one more to match his total from the entirety of 2025-26. So, he seems to be ageing like a fine French wine. All that’s needed is a final push on the contract front to continue an undoubtedly happy marriage.

#1493. On The Road: From Hagi and Popescu to Danny Armstrong... football in Bucharest has history and hope

Published: 16:31 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 12:42 EDT, 2 November 2026

The Starbucks at the entrance to the Old Town makes a familiar point by its very presence. The Half-Time Bar roars a modern truth incessantly.

Bucharest 2026, beneath the enduring glitz of imperial time and amid the clinging grip of post-communism, has become marked by globalism.

Starbucks serves its universal wares and the Half-Time Bar resounds to the English Premier League. Yet the fabulous gems of Romanian football are not far away.

The Muzeul Fotbalului sits on the edge of the Old Town. It is starkly modern. Its four floors offer strips to buy, interactive displays to goggle at and fiddle with, and shirts to admire or even covet. There are strips worn by Maradona, Pele, Cruyff and Ronaldo. But there is Romanian history too.

Gheorghe Hagi, Gheorghe Popescu and Cristian Chivu are rightly celebrated. The wonderful run by the national team to the quarter-finals of the World Cup is recalled in full, glorious colour.

There is a tribute to Helmuth Duckadam, who is the only goalkeeper to have saved four penalties in a Champions League final. When Steaua Bucharest defeated Barcelona in a penalty shoot-out in 1986, since you ask. Incidentally, Miodrag Belodedici is the only Romanian to win the Champions League twice, once with Steaua and then with Red Star in 1991.

Scottish winger Danny Armstrong scored in Dinamo Bucharest's 2-0 win over UTA Arad

'That era is gone. It is not coming back any time soon,' says Jo, dishing out tickets while fielding questions from visitors.

Football was strong under communist rule with star players tied to clubs and only allowed to leave for abroad at the behest of the government. Steaua was the team of the ministry of defence, Dinamo Bucharest was the team of the police. Both ruled the roost. Two years before Steaua won the Champions League, Dinamo lost in the semi-finals.

Now Steaua has been rent asunder. It is now called FCSB after a legal dispute over ownership of its name after a takeover by Gigi Becali. Dinamo have not won the title since 2006. Both seem to be haunted by old glories.

'I am Steaua,' says Jo. 'I always will be. My father was too. He said to me I had a choice: 'Support Steaua or sleep outside'.'

But Jo accepts that the best that can be hoped for is a minor renaissance in the national side.

'Club football at the highest level is simply about money and there is little of that here,' he says.

The verdict is more gloomy from Toni. With desultory glances towards Manchester City against Brighton playing out on multiple screens in the Half-Time Bar, the student says: 'The only team we have in European football this season is Universitatea (of Craiova). The others went out in qualifying. Steaua, for example, could not even qualify for the European Conference League. Universitatea is in that. That's where we are.'

There is no sneering from this Scot. 'Look at your country,' he says. 'Maybe a little bit better but nowhere near what it was.'

Dinamo Bucharest have not won the league for 20 years, but they have a passionate support

Ion, an older gentleman, interjects. 'It is a cabal now,' he says of European competition. 'Maybe good for the TV but only four or five teams outside of England can win it.'

But he adds: 'I am Dinamo. I still go. You will see what it means tomorrow.'

The Sunday game against UTA Arad is certainly compelling. There is a large crowd with an excellent atmosphere. But the cup tie last Wednesday against Chindia Targoviste was instructive for this observer.

It showcased what was still impressive about the Romanian game. It was possible, too, to have conversation with supporters as the cup is not taken too seriously at this stage and the crowd was only a few thousand.

The venue was the National Arena as the Dinamo Stadium is being rebuilt. The National Stadium is a wonderful arena, far better than anything we have to offer in Scotland. On Wednesday, as the rains thundered in Bucharest, the closed roof offered what seemed like a view of the stars but was, in fact, an array of lights peppering the modern protection from elements.

My accent invited conversation. 'Ah, a Scotsman,' muttered a companion in the splendid stand. 'Thank you for coming. It is good that Romanian football can be spoken about elsewhere.'

There was particular pleasure at my identity. 'Danny Armstrong is simply our hero,' says Nick, an engineer, who is at the game with his son and his friend Piti. 'He is the best player in the country and we will enjoy him while we can. Why does he not play for the national team?'

The answer to this is debated but there is no room for argument with Armstrong's impact on the Superliga since his move from Kilmarnock. 'It is not only goals and assists,' says Nick. 'He leads the team so well by his example. He is not in the team tonight because he is too important to risk in this fixture. If we are in trouble, he might come on but I don't foresee this.'

Gheorghe Hagi is among the Romanian legends celebrated at Bucharest's Muzeul Fotbalului

He is right. Dinamo win 5-2 and Armstrong remains on the bench. The player is thus fresh to give Mailsport an exclusive interview the next day. This is coming soon to a sports page near you but no spoiler alert is needed to reveal that the Scot is relishing his opportunity in the Romanian capital.

He is the fans' darling. And Dinamo, despite their recent lack of success, have a strong, impassioned support. 'This club has struggled and we have not won the league for 20 years,' says Piti. 'But there was even once a threat to our existence a few years ago but the fans pulled together.'

He points out that supporters would buy three tickets each for a game just to help Dinamo pay the bills. 'We put everything we could in. I know football is really just bread and circuses so success is not too important to me. But the existence of the club is. That's important.'

Dinamo stood for the opposition to the Ceausescu regime under communism. 'Steaua was run by Nicu, the son of Nicolae, the leader of the country. So it was regarded as the team of the regime and obviously it had strong links to the military. Dinamo was the team many dissenters backed.'

That was then. This is now. The team has strong designs on the title. 'With Danny we can do anything,' says Nick.

This sentiment was reinforced tonight. Armstrong walked on the pitch carrying his two-year-old daughter, Darby. He left to an ovation with minutes remaining, having scored a beautiful opener in their 2-0 victory. These are good days for the player and the fans who love him.

#1492. AC Milan, Inter: how much will the new Milan stadium bring in?

This is a major announcement for the future of AC Milan and Inter. While the two Milanese clubs are preparing the construction of their new stadium, intended to replace the historic San Siro, the name of the future venue is now known. Presented during a press conference organized at the Sforza Castle in Milan, the project officially revealed its main partner: the new stadium will be called “ Generali Stadium », named after the Italian insurance giant. A particularly lucrative commercial agreement since, according to the Italian press, the naming contract should bring in around 650 million euros over a period of twenty years, or an average of 32.5 million euros per season. La Gazzetta Dello Sport. A considerable financial windfall for the two Lombard giants, who are seeking to develop their revenues in order to compete with the greatest European powers. Generali will also become the official partner of the two clubs in the insurance sector.

Scheduled for the 2031-2032 season, the inauguration of this new enclosure will mark an important stage in the history of Milanese football. The future stadium will present an original architecture, with a hexagonal exterior structure and stands arranged in a bowl, raised on a podium. The Generali name will be widely visible on the facade of the building. However, a particularity is planned for European competitions: in accordance with UEFA rules concerning the commercial rights of speakers, the Generali Stadium will take the name ” Milan Stadium » during Champions League matches and other international competitions. An operation already applied to several large European stadiums, notably those of Juventus and Arsenal. With this partnership, Milan and Inter join the list of Italian clubs having sold the naming rights to their venue, like the Allianz Stadium in Turin or Atalanta’s New Balance Arena.

#1489. Allegri banned for Juventus reunion as Napoli lodge appeal

Massimiliano Allegri will not be on the Napoli bench when his side visit the Allianz Stadium on Sunday night. Serie A’s sporting judge has suspended the former Juventus coach for two matches following his dismissal against Roma, although Napoli have confirmed they will challenge the decision.

The ban means one of the most talked about reunions of the autumn could take place without its main character in the dugout, unless the appeal goes Napoli’s way before the weekend.

Allegri was sent off late in Saturday’s 3-3 draw with Roma at the Maradona, reacting furiously after Leonardo Balerdi struck a late equaliser for the visitors. As Football Italia reported, he removed his jacket and walked away before returning and having to be held back by his own staff.

The judge’s ruling, published on Monday and detailed by Sky Sport Italia, goes further than the touchline incident. Allegri was punished for an insulting remark aimed at the match officials in the 90th minute, a seriously disrespectful comment directed at them in the dressing room area afterwards, and aggressive behaviour towards an executive of the opposing club. The first two were noted by the fourth official and the referee, the last by staff working for the federal prosecutor.

On top of the suspension, the 59-year-old has been fined €10,000.

The two games Allegri is set to miss are both away from home. Napoli travel to Monza in the midweek round on Wednesday 28 October, before heading to Turin to face Juventus on Sunday 1 November, with both matches kicking off at 20:45 local time.

If the ban stands, his first game back on the bench would be the home fixture against Lazio on Sunday 8 November.

Official SSC Napoli (@sscnapoli) October 26, 2026

Napoli moved quickly. In a short club statement on Monday afternoon, the Partenopei said that, having requested access to the official documents, they would lodge an appeal against the two match suspension handed to their coach.

Sky Sport Italia notes that a successful appeal would open the door for Allegri to take his place on the bench in Turin. Italian reports suggest the case should be heard before the end of the week, so the picture ought to be clear before Sunday.

For Juventus supporters, any meeting with Allegri carries extra weight. He led the club across two spells, the second of which ended in May 2024, and he remains one of the most successful coaches in its history.

Luciano Spalletti’s side head into the week in a better mood after ending a 35 day wait for a league win with the 2-0 victory at Lecce, which lifted them to seventh on 14 points. Douglas Luiz was among the scorers that night, as covered in our report on his first goal for the club.

Whether or not Allegri is in the dugout, Napoli will arrive as a dangerous opponent. You can follow every twist in his relationship with the Bianconeri on our Massimiliano Allegri page.

Sources: Sky Sport Italia, SSC Napoli, Football Italia

#1488. Stephen Robinson proud of his battling Dons but injury crisis deepens

Published: 17:30 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 14:43 EDT, 2 November 2026

Aberdeen boss Stephen Robinson has revealed his injury crisis has become even more catastrophic ahead of the weekend league visit of Hibernian that has the potential to make or break his reign.

The Dons manager saw his side put in a fine, disciplined display in going down 1-0 to Rangers in the Premier Sports Cup final, but lost Emmanuel Gyamfi within 15 minutes after he collided with Kim Min-su and also has Brad Lyons battling a knock.

Robinson admitted afterwards that there is no chance of longer-term absentees Chris Cadden, Mats Knoester and Lewis Mayo being available, with Dan Happe the only player likely to return for the Saturday night showdown with Premiership bottom dogs Hibs after being suspended last night.

‘Gyamfi will be out for a long period of time,’ reported Robinson. ‘It looked like it was maybe the other thigh that he’s had a problem with. It’s a heartbreaker for the boy.

‘Brad Lyons took a really bad knock. I’m not sure how serious that is. Hopefully, he’s got away with it.

‘Chris Cadden will be out for six weeks. Mats Knoester is four to six weeks.

Emmanuel Gyamfi limped off early with an injury in Aberdeen's semi-final defeat

‘The only plus point is Dan Happe. It’s very difficult because half the squad are not available. Any team that does well, there’s consistency and patience.

‘Over time, the last person that had prolonged success in Aberdeen was Derek (McInnes). He was given a lot of time and a lot of support, but we’ve not been able to put a consistent team, never mind a consistent shape, on the pitch.

‘It’s four changes every week at the moment.’

Robinson, however, stated his pride in the way his players performed and backed centre-back Jack Milne while taking a pop at the criticism he has come in for of late.

‘They rose against adversity this time. They put in a real performance,’ he said.

‘Rangers scored during our best spell in the game, which is unfortunate, but it’s been a tough week for us with injuries, really tough.

‘They showed great character and courage.

‘Jack’s a young man. Surprisingly, he’s from Aberdeen and he still gets an incredible amount of stick.

‘He’s had one full season and he’s a lovely boy that wants to learn. He’s just learning the game. I thought he showed real character.’

Dons boss Stephen Robinson on the touchline in the 1-0 defeat to Rangers

Robinson also refused to criticise captain Kevin Nisbet after seeing him pass up a couple of golden chances.

‘If you want chances to fall to anyone, it’s Kevin and he had the opportunity to play Mitchy Ntelo in with one of them when clean through,’ he reflected.

‘We had grown into the game. We were organised defensively despite not knowing what our team would be until Saturday morning.

‘I’m proud of the players because they gave me absolutely everything.

‘You’d need to ask the fans if they saw positive performances. I can only answer for myself. I saw a group of boys give everything in adversity.

‘Everyone expected us to roll over and get battered but that wasn’t the case. They’ve shown they have the character to play for Aberdeen in big games, no doubt.’

#1487. Premier League: Tottenham tames Chelsea and finally launches its season

Tottenham finally has its benchmark match. After a particularly complicated start to the season, Roberto De Zerbi’s Spurs traveled to Stamford Bridge this Saturday with the ambition of confirming their first success of the season in the Premier League, obtained on the previous day against Coventry (3-1). But the task looked particularly delicate against Chelsea, fourth before the match and winner of the last six London derbies between the two teams in the league. Deprived of João Pedro, Xabi Alonso’s Blues lined up Rogers up front with Quenda, Neto and Palmer behind him while De Zerbi decided to start Mathys Tel on the left side of his attack. A profitable choice in the offensive animation of the visitors, who quickly displayed a much more attractive face than during their previous outings.

Because contrary to expectations, Tottenham took control of the game from the first minutes. The Spurs increased the sequences of possession and collective movements, with a particularly inspired James Maddison between the lines. Mohammed Kudus first tried his luck without finding the target, before Chelsea responded with Cole Palmer, whose shot was brilliantly saved by Antonín Kinský (15th). But the biggest chance of the first act went to Omar Marmoush. Perfectly served behind by Andrew Robertson after a combination with Mathys Tel, the Egyptian striker missed his face-to-face by shooting directly at Mike Penders (30th). Very restless, Tel also caused problems for Acheampong on his side, actively participating in the domination of Spurs. Despite several interesting situations, the two teams returned to the locker room with a goalless draw.

Returning from the locker room, Tottenham continued to show good intentions, despite the injury exit of James Maddison, replaced by Conor Gallagher. Chelsea tried to regain control of the proceedings, but the visitors maintained a real collective solidity while continuing to project themselves forward. And the efforts of Roberto De Zerbi’s men were finally rewarded in the 77th minute. On a corner hit by Mateus Fernandes, Mike Penders completely missed his aerial intervention under pressure from Jan Paul van Hecke, sending the ball into his net himself (0-1). A huge blow for the Blues, whose evening changed again three minutes later with the expulsion of Cole Palmer. Already warned in the first period, the England international received a second yellow card after a sole on Conor Gallagher (80th), leaving his partners at ten for the final minutes.

In numerical superiority, Tottenham then sought to make the break. Gallagher notably created a good opportunity, repelled by Penders, before Sandro Tonali sent his recovery over the top (85th). Mathys Tel also continued to provoke on his wing before being rewarded. On a solitary rush, he came to offer the second goal to his team. Solid until the end, Spurs preserved their advantage to win at Stamford Bridge (0-2) and end a series of six consecutive defeats against their London rival in the championship. A major success which allows Tottenham, sixteenth before this eighth day, to leave the red zone and distance themselves from the last places. Conversely, Chelsea are letting precious points slip away in the race for first places. Above all, Roberto De Zerbi finally saw his team combine collective mastery, quality of play and defensive efficiency. Enough to look forward to the rest of the season with greater optimism.

#1486. Former Geordie Guimaraes taunts Sunderland fans as Arsenal show mark of champions

Bruno Guimarães cupped his ears and had a plastic cup thrown at him as the abuse came down from the stands. Despite the missiles, the Brazilian wore a look that made it clear he was very much enjoying his first goal in an Arsenal shirt.

Mikel Arteta has laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality. Late meals and making the dressing room hotter are among his tricks, although nothing can prepare a player having 40,000 fans calling you a “sad Geordie b------”.

So it was a sweet moment for Guimarães, even more so after coming just after Sunderland had a penalty saved. Just 121 seconds after Enzo Le Fée had his spot kick tipped on to a post by David Raya, Guimarães was rubbing salt into the wound with a stunning long-range strike that went in off the crossbar.

Enzo Le Fée is denied by David Raya from the spot 😳🧤📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/wnoMCDVh88

Bruno Guimarães silences the Stadium of Light with a BEAUTY 🥵🚀📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zQHSSLxC3o

The former Newcastle captain gave the perfect response after being taunted his old rivals. “It was a beautiful goal,” he said. “Everyone knows my past, I had an amazing history at Newcastle. But now I’m trying to create a new history here and I have started on the right foot.”

What an important week it has been for Arsenal, who have shown their squad depth by winning in Napoli then travelling to the Stadium of Light and extending their perfect start to the season to six games.

Other teams with aspirations of the title dropped points earlier in the day, while Arteta could battle to a win with key players brought back into the team and Guimarães coming off the bench at half-time. A trip in the Champions League followed by an away game the following weekend is a barometer of where teams are, and Arsenal have sounded a warning after coming through a bruising encounter.

Régis Le Bris’s team offer a challenge that is impossible to replicate, even by the standards of Arteta’s “sabotage” to make his players uncomfortable. Fans belted out Elvis Presley and 90s anthem Ready To Go just before kick-off. Then there was the aggression that Arsenal players faced. There were complaints of elbows being aimed at Gabriel Magalhães.

Bukayo Saka scored a stoppage-time penalty to seal the win but the evening belonged to Guimarães, the £75m summer signing who has been waiting for this moment to ignite his Arsenal career.

“Everyone knows I had a difficult start through injuries in my short time. But I’m glad to be back and glad to play,” Guimarães said. “I feel very good. It was unbelievable to score a beautiful goal, beautiful moment for me and my family and I am happy.”

These are ominous signs for Arsenal’s title rivals, with Guimarães’s return to fitness adding to the midfield options. Arteta’s changes to his starting line-up restored Riccardo Calafiori and Kai Havertz – two of the in-form players in the Premier League – to the team, rather than squad players being rotated.

And his players stood up to a physical challenge. Brian Brobbey used his frame to back into the Arsenal’s centre-backs, who are unlikely to given such a tough assignment this season aside from facing Erling Haaland.

Guimarães was brought on at half-time along with Jurriën Timber, which was another sign of Arsenal mounting a strong defence of their title. With Arteta’s changes altering the pace of the game, the match turned just before the hour mark. John Brooks saw nothing in the incident that floored Gabriel at a corner, but at the next set-piece penalised Ezri Konsa for wrestling with Dan Ballard, much to Arteta’s fury.

Le Fée had earned a point against Brentford a week earlier with a penalty, but this time his finish was tipped on to the post by David Raya. “We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that,” added Arteta.

“But I loved the save from David, the way the team reacted, the way we go again and we go against everything, but this should never happen, it’s not fair, and I am sad, very sad, in that sense.”

Raya also denied Nordi Mukiele from close range when Granit Xhaka’s expertly taken free-kick found his team-mate in front of goal. Sunderland have their own European campaign starting on Thursday and will start with confidence after pushing the champions all the way.

Brooks awarded a penalty in stoppage-time when Saka was brought down by Reinildo Mandava, who was dismissed. “I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place,” added Arteta.

Bukayo Saka wraps up all three points for Arsenal from the spot 🥶📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrLyrykwlh

Mikel Arteta launched a furious attack on referee John Brooks for awarding a penalty against Arsenal and fears similar decisions will cost his team the Premier League title.

Brooks gave a spot-kick for Ezri Konsa tussling with Dan Ballard, although Arteta accused the Sunderland centre-back of a “judo roll”.

Enzo Le Fée’s penalty was saved by David Raya, with Arsenal winning after goals from Bruno Guimarães and Bukayo Saka.

“In my opinion, that is not acceptable. I watched it 20 times,” said Arteta. “And I cannot find a way to understand how you think to give a penalty in that situation or the way the VAR has to intervene.

“I’m sad that we have to discuss something in such a beautiful game at this level. That has gravity because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship. And at this level, with all the work that we put in, this cannot happen.

“You see, it is a judo roll and it brings the player on the floor. So how can this happen? I cannot find an explanation. That’s why I’m trying to find that.”

The win rounded off a positive week for Arsenal despite Arteta’s fury at the officials.

“I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place. We had really good periods but didn’t score and after that they can suffocate you especially when they decided to be really physical and very direct and we had to overcome a situation that in my opinion was absolutely unacceptable at this level. I’m very worried and very sad because this can never be a penalty ever.

“Are you surprised? Are you surprised? No. OK.

“Ezri does nothing. Just watch it. We have a lot of cameras and VAR, and we have to take responsibility to protect the game. Today the game was unprotected and it could have cost us the game and the momentum which is a really, really serious thing,” he added.

“I’m making it very clear publicly because it’s for the game, it’s not only for Arsenal, this cannot happen at this level. We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that.”

Guimarães’s goal was his first for Arsenal, with Arteta adding: “Beautiful, he came on, the goal, the assist, remarkable. That why we talk about the finishers and making that impact and being able to support and help the team. He was outstanding.”

Three points or not, the Arsenal manager is furious about the penalty that was awarded to Sunderland.

I’m so upset – it’s unacceptable at this level. Unacceptable. This can change the course of a season, of the championship. I’ve seen it 10 times, to make sure, because I saw it live and said ‘It’s not possible at this level it can be a penalty’. Because it’s a judo roll, that’s what it is. It cannot happen.

I’ve been in football for 27 or 28 years - it’s not a penalty in any game, in any league, in any context.

Sunderland are a really, really good team and I don’t want to take any credit away from them. It’s been extremely tough and I’m really happy that we’ve done it.

"It's not a penalty in any case, in any game, in any context, in any league" 😳Mikel Arteta reflects on Arsenal's 2-0 win over Sunderland 👀@jules_breach | 📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/2BUZILexk3
