#1435. James Milner runs New York Marathon in three hours and nine minutes - just months after retiring from football at 40 - after using AI training programme

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 07:49 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 07:49 EDT, 2 November 2026

James Milner may only be a few months retired as a professional footballer, but he showcased he is still an elite athlete after partaking in his first-ever marathon at the weekend.

Milner swapped his football boots for his running shoes on Sunday as he competed in the New York Marathon.

And the 40-year-old clocked an impressive time running the 26.2-mile route on his debut at three hours, nine minutes and four seconds.

The former Leeds, Newcastle, Aston Villa, Manchester City, Liverpool and Brighton midfielder was running for the James Milner Foundation - which has raised over £1.3million previously for various charities such as the NSPCC and Help for Heroes.

And speaking ahead of the race, Milner revealed that he had been using AI as his main training-base tool.

Asked about his long run in preparation for the New York Marathon, the former England international told Let's Run: 'Longest I've done is just over 32 kilometers. I hit 30 another couple of times, and then just used AI really for a training program.

James Milner ran the New York Marathon in three hours, nine minutes and four seconds

Milner only retired from football at the end of last season, finishing his career at Brighton

He won 11 major honours in his career, including the Champions League at Liverpool in 2018-19

'That's how it started, yeah. I know a few other people and stuff, but yeah, just bounced things off that really and went from there.'

It is unclear if all-time Premier League appearance holder Milner (658 games), who turns 41 in January, will run another marathon again in the future - but when that prospect was proposed to him, he revealed the training for it has helped him adjust to the realities of no longer playing professionally.

'I think it's one of them, after I've finished - hopefully - on Sunday, I'll either love it and have the bug and want to tick off loads of marathons, or maybe I'll hate it, never want to do another and maybe go to some triathlons or something else,' he continued.

'But fitness has always been a big part of my life, and I feel I've always been goal-orientated. I think I'd find it hard to not have a goal to train for, and I think this has been really important for me in terms of retiring and having something to aim for and training and still having that importance.

'Even when I was on holiday, [it was like] look, I need to get up and train for this. I need to eat the right things because I've got this run in the morning. I've lived that for 25 years. It's important for me to keep that going, and I feel very fortunate to be part of the New York Marathon. It's such a special city every time you're here.'

During a storied career, Milner won the Premier League twice with Manchester City before lifting the title as well as the Champions League with Liverpool.

In total Milner, who also had a loan spell at Swindon, won 11 major honours during his career alongside 61 England caps.

Michael Carrick doesn’t feel like he is on his last legs as Manchester United head coach – but admits people might think he is ‘crazy’ for looking forward to the Champions League clash with Roma at Old Trafford on Tuesday night.

Speaking ahead of the game at Carrington on Monday, Carrick also insisted that he has no concerns over Lisandro Martinez’s commitment despite the Argentine’s reckless red card at Chelsea on Saturday.

United go into the game against Roma in danger of equalling a club record of ten consecutive games without a win in a single season set by Dave Sexton’s team in March 1978.

Last week, United bosses gave Carrick more time to turn the season, but there is a growing suspicion that he could be sacked in the international break after the next two games against Roma and Aston Villa.

Asked if he has the same feeling, Carrick said: ‘No, not at all. Listen. I can’t look into the future, and you never know what's going to happen. I don't know what's going to happen.

‘That doesn't change the way I feel. That doesn't change how we're preparing for the game tomorrow, and I'm actually really looking forward to the game. I can't wait for the game tomorrow.

Michael Carrick does not feel like he is on the brink of the sack at Manchester United

'You might think I'm crazy with the results we've had and what's going on, but I genuinely, really can't wait for the game tomorrow, and that's all I'm focused on, really I am.

‘Whatever happens, it is going to happen, but we want to make it a big night tomorrow night first.

‘It's what I am, it's what I live for, you know. A lot of people could do my job when you're winning a lot of football games. It's about finding the solutions, finding the answers, staying strong, leading right and getting the best out of the players.

‘We've got to keep pushing for that. But it doesn't change my mindset at all. I love being here, I love working with the players, and the struggles and the challenges, that just drives you on to want it even more.’

Martinez is available to face Roma but will be banned for the Villa game on Sunday after he was sent off for two bookings in the space of 82 seconds at Stamford Bridge – earning the second yellow card for striking Wesley Fofana in the face.

It followed the Argentine’s outburst against club bosses, and director of football Jason Wilcox in particular, after United were beaten by Atletico Madrid last month.

However, Carrick insisted there are no concerns over Martinez’s commitment or the general discipline in the dressing-room after Bruno Fernandes criticised his tactics in the defeat to Como a fortnight ago.

‘No, I've got no concerns about commitment at all,’ said Carrick. ‘Things happen in football. Sometimes you do things, sometimes you make a decision, sometimes you make mistakes, sometimes it goes well for you. But the commitment is not an issue for sure.

‘The dressing room is a good, good place, so perceptions are a funny thing. They can make things look all sorts of different ways and think about all sorts of different things. I've said it before, the commitment of the players to the club, to me, to each other, I don't question that at all. We need to play better, we can make better decisions, but commitment's not a thing at all.’

He says he is excited for Tuesday's Champions League clash against Roma - despite the potential for another embarrassment

Martinez and Fernandes are out of contract in June, although United have an option to extend both by 12 months. They are in talks with Fernandes but Martinez faces a more uncertain future at Old Trafford.

‘You know how discussions go and when anything's finalised, we'll let you know. But at this stage, there's nothing any further to update really,’ said Carrick.

Patrick Dorgu returned to training at Carrington on Monday after six weeks out of action but the Dane won’t be involved against Roma. Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford missed the session and will remain on the sidelines with Benjamin Sesko and Manuel Ugarte.

United badly need a win after picking up three points from their first three games against Sabah, Atletico Madrid and Como. They sit 20th in the league phase. After Roma, they face Sporting Lisbon, RB Leipzig, Bayern Munich and Villarreal.

‘Of course we're looking for the win,’ said Carrick. ‘There is the bigger picture and it’s about getting through to the later stages. One or two games you can get away with really, as long as you make amends for that. Tomorrow and the games coming up are going to dictate that for us. So we're certainly still in it with a great chance of progressing, and it's got to be the focus for now.’

Roma’s only defeat in all competitions this season came in a dramatic 4-3 collapse to Real Madrid in the Champions League. But they have lost on all four of their visits to Old Trafford including a 7-1 defeat in 2007 – when Carrick scored twice – and 6-2 in 2021.

‘Long time ago, eh?’ smiled Carrick. ‘It was a magical night, I have to say. It was one of the best nights, one of the best games, one of the best atmospheres I've been fortunate enough to witness.

‘So the fact that I scored a couple and that was very unusual gives me great, great memories. But it was more the whole emotion of the night really. I have to say that it was a special one.’

After a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

Brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. Carrick and his analysts will rewatch the footage of all three goals in horror at how they conceded.

Erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. Sunday’s trip to Fulham before the international break now feels like a big game for United and Carrick.

“We’ve gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that,” Carrick said. “I’ll be honest about that, that’s how it feels, but it doesn’t have to be like that. If we win football matches again, it can go in a different direction.

“We have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches.

“It doesn’t feel good at the moment. It doesn’t feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win quickly. The next game is Sunday. That’s all I’m thinking about right now.”

At the start of the evening it seemed that the tie would be remembered for Lacey scoring on his first start for United, the first teenager to do so since Marcus Rashford. In the week when JJ Gabriel, one of United’s great academy talents, asked to leave the club, a different United teenager was kissing the badge when he found the net.

SHEA LACEY ON HIS FIRST START!!! 🔴🌟What a hit from the 19-year-old to open the scoring for Man Utd! pic.twitter.com/Ex2ceXaUge

Gross took his chance when United carelessly played the ball out of defence again, with Diogo Dalot’s clearance mishit. Luka Vuskovic’s header went straight into the United penalty area, with their centre-backs failing to react quickly enough.

Pascal Gross takes advantage of a gifted opportunity to level the score! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/Qu2E0B6060

“We take it how it is. For Carrick, matches such as this can define a United manager’s reign if he cannot turn results around. The image of Ruben Amorim in the dugout at Grimsby was one of the lasting impressions of last season before Carrick was brought in to salvage the campaign.

“We can’t put ourselves in that position after being ahead in the game and the game finishing like it did,” he said. “So we’ve got to react to it. We’ve got another game on Sunday, we’ve got to react to it.”

The start of the game and the end of the game was completely different, didn’t feel like the same game or the same emotions at all. We had the game exactly where we wanted it and let it get away from us in a big way.

Boos ring around Old Trafford. For the first time in 50 years, they lose a game at Old Trafford after leading 2-0. Another proud record falls in the post-Ferguson era.

Brighton have now won five of their last six games at Old Trafford, and are one of the best front-footed sides in the league on form.

As United push everyone forward, Heaven is penalised for a push on Vuskovic, and that is surely that now.

Mbeumo tees up Fernandes for a Hail Mary from 25 yards but he balloons the shot miles over the bar. Brighton fans can see the finish line and a place in the fourth round now.

Five minutes of added time to play, but Brighton have a corner after their press ensnares Tielemans on the edge of United’s defensive third. Dalot got a toe to the ball to prevent Rutter a sight at goal. Darlow claims the delivery, but some time has ticked away.

Tielemans slices his cross over the bar while off balance. This would be the first time since 1976 that United have led 2-0 in a game at Old Trafford and gone on to lose. At the moment, an equaliser does not look to be on its way.

Old Trafford growing impatient with how slowly United are moving the ball, a lack of options for the player in possession and they are being caught on it repeatedly by a sharp Brighton team.

Diego Gomez really should have sealed the victory, picked out by another clever Gross pass, but with so much time to take aim he blasted straight at Darlow. United still alive in the tie, but only just.

Lovely Brighton interplay again, Gross just keeps making the right decision around the box. This time his cut-back finds Kostoulas but Yoro blocks his goal-bound shot. Now Brighton make their fifth change: Rutter replaces Kostoulas.

Brighton still swinging punches. Costinha swings in a teasing cross to the back post, headed down by Gross, but De Cuyper cannot get over his volley. Carrick has made his final change: Cunha is on for Rashford.

Big miss by Rashford, but a big save from Jason Steele. It was a lovely touch by Fernandes while half stumbling that released Rashford, and he had so much time to think when through against the goalkeeper, but Steele stuck out a right boot to save.

Hurzeler making two more Brighton changes: Ayari and Kadioglu on for Hadjam and Boscagli, which probably makes their XI on the pitch even stronger. Kadioglu was voted Brighton’s player of the season for 2025-26.

Sesko with space to drive forward and look to pass or shot, but he dallies and dawdles before losing possession, much to the frustration of Old Trafford. Sesko has looked short of sharpness and confidence so far.

Delicious pieces of skill from Lacey, a Cruyff turn against the touchline when he was facing away from goal. Hadjam thought he had the winger boxed in, and dragged him down at the expense of a yellow card. Crowd enjoyed that.

Vuskovic with a shot from distance which is always rising; a number of Brighton players have tried their luck from range tonight, perhaps inspired by Lewis Dunk’s screamer at Coventry. This second half has a been a bit of a non-event thus far.

Matt O’Riley clips Heaven, which enabled the United defender to get out jail because he did not have control of the ball and was scrambling. Rashford has been a bright spark for United, but he is having to do too much of the heavy lifting on his own at the moment. This time he finds Lacey on the overlap, but his cross is volleyed clear. Brighton continue to apply the squeeze, but Kostoulas fouls Mazraoui to enable Darlow to boot the ball long and United to push up the pitch. Carrick’s team are still not exerting much control on the contest, though.

That is something of a rarity at this stage of the League Cup.

Plenty of entertainment for the paying punters at Old Trafford, with Shea Lacey and Mason Mount scoring twice in two minutes to put United in a commanding position. Given the JJ Gabriel story, the home fans enjoyed seeing a 19-year-old kiss the badge after scoring on his full debut.

Brighton have probably been the better team in general play though, and scored a deserved goal on the stroke of half-time.

United’s second-string back four looking very shaky, understandably.

Carrick and United wanted a foul on Sesko on halfway, but the referee said nothing doing. Hadjam then floats a diagonal pass over the head of Heaven to find the run of Kostoulas, but goalkeeper Darlow surely had the chance to come off his line and claim? Clean hit from almost 35 yards from Boscagli, but his left-footed attempt whistles just over the bar. Yoro heads away a temping Gross cross when Brighton had three blue shirts in promising positions. Rashford then puts the ball through the legs of Chema Andres, and United have a corner.

Lacey goes down hoping for free-kick, anticipating the contact from Gross but it was not forthcoming. Since 2013-14, United have been 2-0 up at Old Trafford 145 times, winning 143 and drawing just two.

Brighton well on top now, and Ayden Heaven goes to ground hoping for a free-kick but the referee is having none of it. O’Riley’s cross is turned behind for a corner, which United scramble away. Feels like a Brighton goal is on the way, despite the comfortable scoreline for United.

Brighton’s corner swung in from the right was far too deep and loopy, drifting harmlessly behind for a United goal kick. Mazraoui is now back on the pitch but he does not look 100 per cent. Brighton enjoying some long passages of possession now, but you sense United are happy to drop off and let them have the ball. More promising build-up play ends with Mazraoui heading a cross over the bar for a Brighton corner.

There has been a lengthy stoppage in play while Mazraoui receives treatment for a bang on the head. United’s left-back looks a little shaken and is off the pitch now, and Mason Mount has dropped into the left-back position.

Sesko and Vuskovic are enjoying a good battle early on. Andrey Santos then sells Tielemans a little short in midfield and Brighton take advantage, but O’Riley does not have the pace to get away from Mazraoui.

There are usually chances at both ends when Brighton are involved and so it has proved so far. A pleasant surprise for any Manchester United fans who feared the worst arriving at Old Trafford tonight.

Brighton playing their way into trouble in their own defensive third, and it is great work from Rashford to drive into the penalty area from the left. Steele makes a save with his feet, but the ball runs kindly for Mount to power his shot into the ground and into the roof of the net.

Mason Mount DOUBLES Man Utd's lead! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/c83ggCb8Bf

The 19-year-old, sent off against Brighton in the FA Cup last season, has powered a left-footed shot from the edge of the box beyond Steele. That is a moment to lift the Old Trafford crowd.

Really slick, one-touch football from Brighton through midfield, players bumping off passes blind around the corner knowing their team-mate has read the next move, but the move breaks down at the edge of the box. Brighton knocked United out of the FA Cup in the third round, with Danny Welbeck scoring at Old Trafford, meaning the club played just 40 matches in 2025-26.

Carrick will want to make a better fist of the cup competitions, but he could really use a win of any kind after taking just four points from United’s first four league games of the new season.

#1432. Heartwarming moment Luis Suarez spots former Liverpool team-mate's son - now Chelsea academy starlet - and poses for a photo

Published: 08:34 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 10:14 EDT, 2 November 2026

Luis Suarez shared a heartwarming moment with former Liverpool team-mate Glen Johnson's son Kobi while at Inter Miami's training complex in Fort Lauderdale.

The 39-year-old Uruguayan was at the ground for the Messi Cup, a youth tournament the MLS side is hosting, and spotted Kobi Johnson lining up with the rest of the Chelsea Under-14s, who are competing in the United States.

The former Liverpool and Barcelona striker went over to the youngster and said: 'I used to play with your dad, I've known you since you were little.'

The one-time Champions League winner then smiled for a photograph with the youngster.

When asked about the chance encounter, teenage Johnson said: 'He (Suarez) just said like, he remembers when I was a little boy and I was quite chubby, and then he asked for a photo.'

Johnson has been at Chelsea from the under-eights and has risen through the ranks, steadily gaining a reputation as an exciting young talent.

Suarez shared a sweet moment with Glen Johnson's son Kobi at Inter Miami's training ground in the US

Kobi Johnson is currently on the books at Chelsea where he is tipped to follow his father into professional football

Suarez and Johnson spent four seasons together at Liverpool between 2011 and 2015

And it is clear to see where he gets it from, with his father Glen having played 357 Premier League games at Chelsea, Liverpool, Portsmouth and Stoke, even winning the league with Chelsea in 2005 and 2006.

It was at Liverpool, however, where the right-back played with Suarez for four seasons between 2011 and 2015 - with the pair were part of a memorable Liverpool team that narrowly missed out on the title back in 2014 after the famous 'Gerrard slip' at Stamford Bridge.

It was during that period too that Suarez was accused of racially abusing former Manchester United left-back Patrice Evra during a Premier League grudge match between the two clubs in 2011.

Suarez was subsequently banned for eight matches after it was ruled that he had used racist language towards Evra.

Johnson controversially publicly defended him at the time, and years later, continued to be conflicted over the incident.

Speaking on talkSPORT in 2019, Johnson said: 'Carra (former team-mate Jamie Carragher) was right to apologise and I'd have to agree with him; I think the timing of it was wrong as the ban was so close.

'But in the club's defence, they were just trying to support one of their players.

'I don't think anyone in that dressing room or at the club believed Luis was racist or capable of being racist.'

While 42-year-old Johnson is enjoying his retirement after leaving the professional game for good in 2018, Suarez is still plying his trade in America at Inter Miami alongside other Barcelona legends like Sergio Busquets and Lionel Messi.

First there was Golden Balls... now there's Golden Bells!

England midfielder Jude Bellingham is starring in an eye-catching underwear campaign for Calvin Klein - almost two decades after David Beckham signed a famous £20m deal to become the face of Emporio Armani.

Real Madrid star Bellingham, one of the stars of England's World Cup campaign, shot the campaign for the fashion giants in the Spanish capital.

The 23-year-old posed in a series of pictures wearing the Icon Cotton Stretch underwear - which retail at around £44 for a pack of three.

'I really enjoyed working on this campaign,' said Bellingham. 'I liked the idea of "the icon underneath" – that confidence starts with feeling comfortable in yourself.'

His underwear campaign follows on from that of fellow Real Madrid and England star Beckham - famously labelled Golden Balls by his wife Victoria.

Beckham signed a three-year deal with Emporio Armani in 2007, shortly after moving to LA Galaxy, with the company revealing sales went up 20 per cent once the news was announced.

Jude Bellingham models the Calvin Klein briefs in a series of images released today

'Calvin Klein is such an iconic brand, so it was great to bring that idea to life in my own way.'

David Beckham models Armani underwear in an advert seen at Macy's in San Francisco

Bellingham celebrated his 50th goal for Real Madrid with a strike against Racing Santander

Bellingham scored his 50th goal for Real on Sunday, in his fourth season at the club since joining from Borussia Dortmund.

The star, who began his career at Birmingham City, netted in a 3-0 win at Racing Santander.

Wearing the No5 shirt in which Zinedine Zidane made his name, Bellingham has now scored one more goal than the great Frenchman for Madrid — in 76 fewer matches.

It comes after he scored seven goals at the World Cup - setting a record for the number scored in one tournament by an England player. It included the final goal in the third-place playoff against France, which England won 6-4.

'Reaching 50 goals with Real Madrid is very special,' said Bellingham. 'Not only for me and my dreams but also for the team.'

'It’s very important for all players to score goals and make a difference in games.'

#1430. Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

This particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

So to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

“I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba said. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”

Floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

As impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy

“It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca said. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”

Allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has said supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was important for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca said.

Cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

All told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

With the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:

Erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

Great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

Mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

Samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

Big cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

What a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

And Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:

And without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

Credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

As we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

Samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

And the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

Samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

He has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

Norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic shows some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

Kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

Norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

It’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:

Man City XI: Rulli; O’Reilly, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Lewis; Kovacic (c), Bouaddi; Ait-Nouri, Cherki, Allan; Samba

Subs: Anderson, Braithwaite, Donnarumma, Fernández, Guéhi, McAidoo, Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes, Semenyo

Norwich City XI: Grimshaw; Yongwa, Bruno Alves, Darling (c), Fisher; Field, Wright; Diallo, Ben Slimane, Crnac; Kvistgaarden

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré

"It's part of the decision that I took when I decided to join this club"Enzo Maresca responds to the doubts surrounding him filling Pep Guardiola's shoes 👇 pic.twitter.com/o6eUjQUOnU

David 🆚 Goliath 🤝🎥 https://t.co/5YXw2tQvfX pic.twitter.com/fTp9zD0xiX

As Abdukodir Khusanov makes his fourth start of the season, Hugo Viana, Man City director of football, has been speaking about the young Uzbek. The 22-year-old signed a new five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

"Abdukodir Khusanov will be one of the best centre-backs in the world" - Hugo Viana 🇺🇿🌏Full interview 🔗 https://t.co/dk3Qi8DF8D pic.twitter.com/hHdVdX5HSF

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

Speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

His older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

City fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

Checking in 🚌🚶‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/xWYGyaH7TY

Ⓒ Darling with the armband🧤 Grimshaw in goal⚡️ Ante on the rightYour Yellows for this evening ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/znOGtvyJyk

Your City side to take on Norwich 👊XI | Rulli, Lewis, Khusanov, Reis, O'Reilly, Bouaddi, Kovačić (C), Samba, Allan, Aït-Nouri, CherkiSUBS | Donnarumma, Anderson, Guéhi, Ndiaye, Fernández, Nunes, Semenyo, McAidoo, Braithwaite🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/LCA4WfACBf

Good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

These two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

Philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

#1429. Rare and common genetic variants shape single-cell immune gene expression

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Understanding the genetic basis of gene expression can shed light on the regulatory mechanisms underlying complex traits and diseases1,2. Single-cell-resolved measures of RNA levels and single-cell expression quantitative trait loci have revealed genetic regulation that drives cell states and types across diverse tissues3. Here we describe phase 1 of TenK10K, which leverages single-cell RNA sequencing data from more than 5 million cells across 28 immune cell types, along with matched whole-genome sequencing data from 1,925 individuals. This provides power to detect associations for rare and low-frequency genetic variants that have largely been uncharacterized in their impact on cell-specific gene expression. We map the effects of both common and rare variants in a cell-type-specific manner using a recent method that increases power by modelling single cells directly rather than aggregated ‘pseudobulk’ counts. We identify putative common regulatory variants for 83% of all 21,404 genes tested and cumulative rare-variant signals for 47% of those genes. We explore how genetic effects vary across cell types and states, develop a framework to determine the degree of single-cell expression quantitative trait loci cell-type specificity and show that about half of the effects are observed only in one or a few cell types. By integrating our results with functional annotations and disease information, we further characterize the likely molecular modes of action for many disease-variant associations. Finally, we explore the effects that genetic variants have on gene expression across continuous cell states, and effects that vary cell-state abundance directly.

Genome-wide association studies (GWASs) have revealed hundreds of thousands of association signals between genetic variants and human diseases and traits4, but the modes of action by which most of these variants affect phenotypes remain to be characterized, especially non-coding variants. The characterization of the impact of genetic variants on gene expression—known as expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) mapping—can help linking variants to the putative genes they regulate1,5,6,7,8,9, thus identifying the genes and pathways involved in disease pathogenesis, which is a critical step in identifying opportunities for therapeutic intervention10.

However, important limitations remain. First, eQTL mapping has traditionally been limited to common genetic variation (minor allele frequency (MAF)) greater than 1–5%) due to relatively small sample sizes and the widespread use of genotyping arrays, which do not accurately genotype most rare variants and complex structural variants11, compared with whole-genome sequencing (WGS) approaches. Second, eQTLs are extremely context specific, with many studies demonstrating that genetic variants frequently affect gene expression levels in ways detectable only in specific tissues3, sorted cell types6,10,12,13 or on stimulation14,15. Single-cell eQTL mapping has further demonstrated that the effects of many genetic variants on gene expression can only be detected within specific cell types and even transient cellular states3,16,17,18,19,20,21,22,23.

Here we introduce phase 1 of the TenK10K (up to 10,000 cells for 10,000 individuals) study, encompassing 5.4 million cells from 1,925 individuals of European ancestry selected from a broader cohort of 2,103 individuals. In accompanying papers, we leverage the same dataset to investigate the effect of tandem repeat variation on gene expression24 and the putative causal links between gene expression measurements and human diseases and traits25, and an overlapping set of samples to explore the impact of genetic variation on chromatin accessibility26.

Here we use an association method we recently developed, SAIGE-QTL27, to map common-variant and rare-variant single-cell eQTLs across immune cell types. We identify more than 150,000 common-variant effects and more than 30,000 rare-variant effects on gene expression, including signals for nearly 5,000 genes (roughly 25%) with no previously reported eQTLs in a large blood eQTL study5. We propose a framework for quantifying the extent of cell-type specificity or sharedness of eQTLs and show that about half of the effects are found in only one or a few cell types, and almost none are ubiquitous across all. We perform statistical colocalization between our eQTLs and 60 disease phenotypes and blood traits, identifying more than 60,000 colocalization events for more than 5,000 genes, providing potential molecular mechanisms in almost 900 genes associated with human phenotypic variation. We use a biologically driven deep learning method, scDeepID, to identify continuous cell states related to cell function and map more than 15,000 eQTLs that vary dynamically along those states. Finally, we identify 164 independent genetic variants that regulate the abundance of cell states.

After quality control, a total of 5,438,679 peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from 1,925 donors were considered for analysis (Fig. 1, Supplementary Table 1 and Methods). We collected and sequenced PBMCs from all individuals, yielding an average of 2,825 cells per individual after quality control (Supplementary Figs. 1 and 2 and Methods).

a, Overview of the data used in this paper introducing phase 1 of the TenK10K cohort. High-quality matched WGS and scRNA-seq data were generated for 1,925 individuals of European ancestry (after quality control). After computational analysis and processing, we conducted both common and rare-variant eQTL analysis and identified cell-type-specific and state-specific effects of genetic regulation in immune cells. We also performed colocalization analysis with GWAS from 60 traits and diseases and mapped QTLs affecting csaQTL. b, Accompanying papers perform complementary analyses using the TenK10K phase 1 cohort. In brief, ref. 25 integrates sc-eQTLs from the present study and 100 GWAS studies to explain the causal role of gene expression in immune cell types across complex traits; ref. 24 uses the WGS data to generate a catalogue of more than 1.7 million polymorphic tandem repeats and dissect their effects on single-cell-resolved gene expression; ref. 26 combines common genetic variants called from WGS with scATAC-seq generated for a subset of roughly 1,000 individuals to investigate the genetic regulation of chromatin accessibility at cellular resolution. c, Schematic of the 28 immune cell types identified, organized by main cell type. d, The number of cells available for analysis by cell type for the 28 immune cell types is summarized in d. Top, bar plot showing total cell numbers per cell type on a log10 scale; bottom, violin plots showing the distribution across individuals on a log10 scale. ASDC, AXL+SIGLEC6+ dendritic cells; cDC1/2, conventional type 1/2 dendritic cells; CD4CTL, CD4+ cytotoxic T cells; dnT,  double-negative T cells; gdT, γδ T cells; ILC, innate lymphoid cells; MAIT, mucosal-associated invariant T cells; pDC, plasmacytoid dendritic cells. Panels created in BioRender: a, Cuomo, A. https://biorender.com/0bkvg8x (2026); c, Cuomo, A. https://biorender.com/fyk570b (2026).

Each cell was assigned to their donor of origin by means of demultiplexing and to an immune cell type using a combined approach of reference-based classification and hierarchical clustering as recommended by the single-cell eQTLGen Consortium28 (Methods). Each cell was assigned to one of 28 different cell types, spanning the key expected immune lineages (Fig. 1c, Supplementary Fig. 3 and Supplementary Table 2).

In addition, we generated WGS data for all 1,925 individuals, which was processed and quality-controlled using established pipelines (Methods). We called 66,658,242 sites across single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and insertions and deletions (indels), of which 53,784,018 (80.6%) were rare (MAF < 1%), roughly 4.5 times as many as from SNP array data (Methods and Supplementary Fig. 4).

To assess the effects of common genetic variation on gene expression changes, we mapped cis eQTLs, testing for the effects of common (MAF > 1%) variant sites within ±100 kilobases (kb) of the gene body on single-cell expression profiles (testing all sufficiently expressed genes; Methods). We used SAIGE-QTL27 to map eQTL effects using single-cell profiles modelled as Poisson counts, rather than relying on ‘pseudobulk’ aggregation. We mapped eQTLs separately in each of the 28 cell types and confirmed the type I error was controlled using permutations (Fig. 2a). At a false discovery rate (FDR) of less than 5%, we identified 154,932 eQTLs in at least one cell type from 17,674 unique eGenes (83% of all genes tested; Fig. 2b and Supplementary Fig. 5). The number of eQTLs identified varied substantially across cell types, largely due to the number of cells available for each cell type and the resulting number of individuals tested affecting statistical power, as previously shown in refs. 16,27 (Fig. 2b, Extended Data Fig. 1 and Supplementary Table 2).

a, Quantile–quantile plot for all common (MAF = 1%, top) and rare (MAF < 1%, bottom) variant eQTL results across 28 immune cell types. For the most abundant cell type, CD4TCM cells, we shuffled individual IDs and reperformed the test to assess calibration (labelled ‘permuted control’). Colour represents cell type, as shown in the legend in the top right. The observed P values are those from the main analysis using SAIGE-QTL (Methods). b, Number of eGenes identified (solid colour) compared to the total number of genes tested (faded) across cell types. Top, common-variant eQTL mapping (single-variant tests); bottom, rare-variant eGenes using combined P values of burden and SKAT tests. The middle bar plots represent the number of cells and individuals available for each cell type to demonstrate their role in the power differences across cell types. For representative cell types, the percentage of eGenes compared to the total number of genes tested is highlighted. Percentages for all cell types are available at Supplementary Table 2. c,d, For all genes with more than one independent signal identified confidently by fine mapping (posterior inclusion probability (PIP) > 0.9, using SuSiE2; Methods) signals (credible sets) were categorized as either primary (including the top most significant variant) or non-primary. Non-primary signals are on average found further away from the gene’s TSS, less likely to be found in promoter regions (c) and more likely in enhancer regions compared with primary signals (d). In c, violin plots represent distribution over n = 17,674 independent signals, and the horizontal lines in the box plots therein represent the first quartile, median and third quartile. e, Proportion of eQTLs identified in each cell type by means of fine mapping, coloured by the number of independent signals (‘only one’ or ‘two or more’).

We performed fine mapping using SuSiE29 (Methods), showing an extra 24,925 (a 16% increase) non-primary (secondary, tertiary and so on)30,31 eQTL signals for 7,131 eGenes (40.4%). We used 95% credible sets to quantify the number of independent signals for each eGene, and explored differences between primary effects (variants from the credible set containing the top variant for each eGene) and non-primary effects (all other credible sets). We find that primary effects contain larger credible sets, and genes in the higher-proportion cell types have substantially more non-primary effects (Fig. 2e and Supplementary Fig. 6). As shown by others31, non-primary signals were found further from the transcription start site (TSS) and more likely in enhancer as opposed to promoter regions (Fig. 2c,d).

We compared the eGenes we identified with those from bulk blood eQTL studies. First, we considered the eQTLGen consortium study5: the largest eQTL study so far in whole blood. We identified a comparable number of eGenes compared to eQTLGen (17,674 and 16,987, respectively), despite the 15-fold smaller sample size (1,925 compared with more than 30,000 individuals; Extended Data Fig. 2a). More than one-quarter of our eGenes were not identified in eQTLGen (n = 4,572, 25.9%); those genes were slightly more lowly expressed, and their expression was more cell-type-specific (Extended Data Fig. 2b,c) compared with eGenes found by both studies; TenK10K-unique eGenes were also more likely to be eGenes in fewer cell types overall, in rare cell types (n < 60,000) compared with more abundant ones or in one cell type only (‘cell-type-specific’, Extended Data Fig. 2d–f), demonstrating the importance of mapping eQTLs at cellular resolution. Conversely, 23% of eQTLGen eGenes were not detected in our study: these were extremely lowly expressed across all 28 cell types (average expression 4% as opposed to roughly 30% for shared eGenes; Extended Data Fig. 2b).

An alternative approach to detect cell-type-specific eQTLs is bulk eQTL mapping on sorted cell types, which has proved to be well-powered even with modest sample sizes. We compared our eQTLs to four such studies (BLUEPRINT6 and CEDAR13, and refs. 10 and 12), matching cell types like for like. Overall, we demonstrate similar to much-increased power to identify cell-type-specific eQTLs, although we note the much larger sample size used in this study. Our study provides assessment of more granular cell types (n = 28) than many previous studies using sorted immune cell types (for example, 13 in ref. 10; Extended Data Fig. 3).

Compared with the OneK1K study16, the previously largest single-cell expression quantitative trait loci (sc-eQTL) map in blood, we identified nearly three times as many eGenes (17,674 compared with 6,469). This reflects several factors, including the increased power from both larger sample size (about twice the individuals: 1,925 compared with 982), number of cells per individual (2,825 compared with 1,291), the consequent more granular cell-type resolution (28 compared with 14 cell types) and the increased power due to modelling single-cell expression profiles rather than pseudobulk. The eGenes identified in our study, rather than OneK1K, were less highly expressed and more likely to be expressed in fewer cell types (in our data; Supplementary Fig. 7).

Finally, to quantify the improvement from cell-type resolution within our data, we compared the eQTLs identified separately in each cell type with a new set of eQTLs obtained from pseudobulk expression values aggregated across all 28 cell types (Methods). At FDR < 5%, this pseudobulk analysis identified 11,359 eGenes, similar to the number found in our most abundant cell type, the CD4+ central memory T (CD4TCM) cells, and nearly 30% fewer than when we consider all eGenes identified in at least one cell type (Extended Data Fig. 4).

We correlated our eQTL effect sizes with promoter-activity scores from PromoterAI32 for each gene’s lead variant across cell types, finding good agreement (median correlation 0.66; Supplementary Fig. 8 and Methods).

Most eQTL studies so far8,9,16,17 have focused on common genetic variants (MAF ≥ 1–5%). Studies investigating the effects of rare variants (MAF < 1%) on tissue-level gene expression7,33 have conducted ‘outlier analyses’, in which rare variants are sought specifically in individuals with extreme expression levels for a given gene rather than performing systematic population-level assessments.

Using SNPs and indels from WGS and SAIGE-QTL, we mapped the effects of rare variation (MAF < 1%) within a cis window (±100 kb) around each gene’s body, using gene-set-based tests for increased power (Methods). For each cell type, we tested for the effects of local rare variants on all sufficiently expressed genes (Methods) using two tests designed to capture different regulatory mechanisms: the burden test, and the sequence kernel association test (SKAT)34.

Overall, we observe 34,376 rare-variant signals across all cell types for 10,005 unique rare eGenes (47% of all genes tested) after FDR correction on the combined P values from the burden and SKAT tests (FDR < 5%; Fig. 2b, Supplementary Fig. 9 and Methods). Type I error was well-controlled for the rare-variant tests (Fig. 2a), and the number of cells per cell type was highly correlated with the number of eGenes identified (correlation 0.98, Extended Data Fig. 1).

Most eGenes were identified by SKAT alone (29,260, 85%), followed by both SKAT and burden (4,975, 14.5%) and burden alone (141, 0.5%). This is consistent with SKAT being more appropriate when variants in the set have mixed direction of effects (that is, some increasing, some decreasing gene expression), which we expect in a regulatory context (Fig. 3a).

a, Bar plot showing the proportion of rare eGenes identified using the different set-based tests—identified as eGenes at FDR < 5% by the burden test, the SKAT test or both—across cell types. b, Number of eGenes identified at P < 10−6 identified when testing for association using only functionally annotated (solid colour) or all-cis (faded colour) rare variants (Methods), using SKAT. Each plot represents a different cell type (n = 26). c, Locus zoom plot of rare genetic variants associated with the SH2D2A gene on chromosome 1 in CD4TCM cells, with the leading genetic variants annotated. LD variants are variants in perfect LD with the annotated putatively causal ones. Bottom plot, zoom in on the chromatin accessibility profile across representative cell types for each main group around the SH2D2A gene and with the top variant (1:156816831:A:AC) shown as a vertical line. The P values shown are from the single-variant tests for rare variants using SAIGE-QTL (Methods). d, Locus zoom plot of rare genetic variants associated with the TMED3 gene on chromosome 15 in NK cells, with the leading splice-altering genetic variant (15:79311418:G:A) annotated. Bottom plot shows AlphaGenome-predicted RNA-seq coverage, splice sites usage and splice sites tracks for exon 1 and 2 of the TMED3 gene for the 15:79311418:G:A variant (ALT, yellow) and reference (REF, green) alleles. Rare eGenes were more ubiquitously expressed across all cell types, whereas common eGenes were expressed in a more cell-type-specific manner (Supplementary Fig. 10a), although this may be partly due to power (Supplementary Fig. 11). Single-variant test results show the expected relationship between allele frequency and effect sizes, with rarer variants showing larger effects on gene expression (Supplementary Fig. 10b). Both common and rare eGenes were enriched for putative promoter activity as estimated by PromoterAI32, with stronger-effect variants being enriched at rare allele frequencies (Supplementary Fig. 10c).

To further characterize our rare-variant signals, we overlapped them with functional annotations from public datasets to characterize genomic regions as putative enhancers, promoters, transcription factor binding sites, DNase sites and others, as well as splice-altering and promoter regions based on SpliceAI35 and PromoterAI32 scores, respectively. Finally, we included cell-type-matched open-chromatin regions using single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq) for a subset of our samples26 (Methods, Extended Data Fig. 5, Supplementary Fig. 12 and Supplementary Table 3).

We performed a second set of gene-level tests focusing only on variants in cell-type-matched open-chromatin regions or in regulatory regions (Methods). Despite reducing the number of variants tested by more than half, this analysis yielded more eGenes across cell types (1.2 times as many eGenes on average, Fig. 3c and Supplementary Fig. 12). This was especially true when weighting variants based on their distance from the TSS of the gene27, probably reflecting the proximity of regulatory regions to the gene. By contrast, when up-weighting rarer variants using the beta(1,25) distribution, the all-cis variant test performed slightly better, possibly because very rare expression-affecting variants are more likely to be coding and thus excluded from our regulatory-focused annotations (Supplementary Fig. 13).

As an example, we identified significant downregulation of SH2D2A in CD4TCM cells (Cauchy combined P value = 1.48 × 10−2), driven by several rare variants in functional regions not previously reported, probably due to their low frequency (MAF < 0.005), highlighting the value of WGS (Fig. 3d). The top variant (1:156816831:A:AC, rs561132719) is a 5′ untranslated region indel overlapping an open-chromatin peak in T and natural killer (NK) cells from scATAC-seq data generated for a subset of our cohort (Fig. 3d, Supplementary Fig. 14 and Methods). The signal is stronger on conditioning on the top common variant for the same gene (conditional P = 2.6 × 10−4). SH2D2A encodes the T cell-specific adaptor protein that induces cytokine production in CD4+ T cells specifically and was linked to autoimmune conditions including hypothyroidism36.

As another example, PRDM4 expression was downregulated by many rare variants across T cell subpopulations, most significantly in CD4+ naive T cells (CD4Naive; P = 1.2 × 10−17). One variant (12:107695720:A:G, rs34017446) was previously reported (in whole blood, with consistent direction of effect5); we also report two new rare(r) variants here. We propose that one of these (12:107761146:T:G, rs71454708; MAF = 0.0099), in high linkage disequilibrium (LD) with 12:107695720:A:G, is probably causal, as it overlaps a CCCTC-binding factor binding site and likely promoter region (Methods), and was predicted to cause expression downregulation (PromoterAI score, −0.77; Extended Data Fig. 6a). PRDM4 encodes a transcription factor that mediates cell proliferation and has been linked to several cancers37.

In some cases, we identified rare variants that probably affect pre-mRNA splicing (n = 126 unique eGenes, with at least one rare variant with SpliceAI score of 0.5 or more, P ≤ 10−6). For 98 of the 126 genes (78%) the effect of the splicing variant on gene expression was detected in only one cell type. However, we observe that roughly 50% of all splicing events come from at least one of the five most abundant cell types (CD4TCM cells, CD4Naive cells, NK cells, CD8+ effector memory T (CD8TEM) cells and CD14Mono cells) suggesting that this is probably an effect of statistical power: we propose that given a better representation of less abundant cell types, we would observe splicing mechanisms to be mostly shared across cell types. We found an association between 15:79311418:G:A (rs141194056) and TMED3 across several cell types (most significantly in NK cells, P = 1.6 × 10−24). This variant (NM_007364.4:c.168+1G>A) is predicted by SpliceAI and AlphaGenome38 to abolish the canonical donor splice site in intron 1, with use of resulting in cryptic donor usage leading to premature termination and nonsense-mediated decay, consistent with the observed reduced expression of TMED3 (both in our data and in AlphaGenome-predicted RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) tracks, Fig. 3e).

Furthermore, the synonymous variant 19:51367458:C:T (rs143501994), was associated with increased CLDND2 expression, with the strongest effects in NK and CD8TEM cells (P = 8 × 10−77 and P = 3 × 10−75 respectively). This variant lies at the penultimate base of exon 3 (NM_152353.3:c.429G>A, p.(Ala143=)). AlphaGenome predicts that it promotes exon 3–4 splicing, reducing intron retention and consequent non-stop decay leading to increased stable CLDND2 transcript abundance, consistent with the single-cell eQTL association direction (Extended Data Fig. 6b).

An important question with single-cell eQTL analysis is the degree to which loci show genetic effects in specific cell types; in other words, how ‘cell-type specific’ are they? For several reasons, this is complex to address directly: genes are variably expressed across cell types, leading to true eQTLs being missed for lowly expressed genes; differences in cell numbers lead to variable power to detect eQTLs across cell types making like-for-like comparison between cell types difficult and LD between loci means we cannot always infer whether alternative top eQTL variants for the same gene in different cells are tagging the same or different causal loci. Existing methods for simultaneously assessing cell-type specificity (such as mash39) are restricted to genes with expression across all conditions, thereby representing only a subset of all expressed genes (Supplementary Fig. 15).

Here we defined five possible scenarios for a given eQTL identified at FDR < 5% in one cell type (cell type A) in pairwise comparison with another cell type (cell type B; Fig. 4a). In scenario 1, the corresponding eGene of the eQTL is not sufficiently expressed (less than 1% cells) in cell type B (specific eGene). In scenario 2, the eGene is sufficiently expressed but no eQTL is identified in cell type B (specific eQTL). Scenario 3 represents a case in which two eQTL variants in low LD (r2 < 0.5) for the same eGene are identified in cell types A and B (distinct eQTL). Conversely, when the same eQTL or an eQTL in LD (r2 ≥ 0.5) for the same eGene are found in cell types A and B, it represents scenario 4 (shared eQTL, concordant effect) when the direction of allelic effect per extra minor allele on gene expression is concordant, or scenario 5 (shared eQTL, discordant effect) when the direction is discordant. To account for power differences when cell type B is rarer, we performed pairwise random-effect meta-analysis and reclassified eQTLs with potential association in cell type B (meta-analysis P < 10−5 × P value in cell type A) as scenario 4 or 5 depending on effect direction concordance (Methods).
